input.raw_content:
Fictional junior Java backend developer with two years of experience building internal business services and supervised student projects. Comfortable translating a small requirement into an API contract, database change, tests and deployment notes. Uses Java, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL and Git in daily development. Looking for a backend role with code review, clear ownership and opportunities to improve reliability. Communicates progress in writing, asks for missing acceptance criteria early and documents limitations rather than presenting unverified assumptions as completed work.

Developed REST endpoints for a fictional inventory application used by an internal training team. Implemented request validation, pagination and role checks with Spring Boot and Spring Security. Designed PostgreSQL tables for products, warehouses and stock movements, added database constraints and reviewed query plans with a mentor. Reduced a report endpoint from approximately 1200 milliseconds to 450 milliseconds in a controlled sample environment by replacing repeated queries with one aggregate query. Wrote JUnit and Mockito tests for validation, permissions and failed transactions. Added structured logs and correlation identifiers so the team could investigate failed requests without logging customer content. Participated in weekly code review, clarified API response fields with a frontend colleague and updated OpenAPI examples before release. Supported a supervised Docker deployment and documented rollback steps; did not own production infrastructure or on-call operations.

Completed a backend internship at a fictional learning organization. Built a task management module with filtering by assignee, status and due date. Used Git branches and pull requests to keep changes small and reviewable. Added integration tests against a disposable PostgreSQL database and corrected timezone handling for task deadlines. Investigated duplicate submissions and introduced an idempotency key for one create endpoint. Compared expected and actual responses with Postman and described reproduction steps in issue reports. Worked with a mentor to understand transactions, indexes and common HTTP error codes. Wrote a short onboarding guide explaining local setup, sample data and how to run the focused tests.

Built a capstone appointment booking service with three other students. Owned backend endpoints for available slots, booking confirmation and cancellation. Prevented double booking with a database uniqueness rule and a transaction rather than a browser-only check. Implemented access and refresh token flows for a demonstration account system. Kept configuration in environment variables and excluded secrets from version control. Containerized the application and database for reproducible local demonstrations. Created sample fixtures for overlapping bookings and permission boundaries. Measured response time with a synthetic dataset and recorded the environment used; the result was a classroom demonstration rather than a production capacity benchmark. Helped write the final API handbook and showed teammates how to reproduce a failed test. Redis was used only for an optional short-lived cache; the database remained authoritative.

Completed a fictional Bachelor of Software Engineering program in 2024. Coursework covered object oriented programming, relational database design, software testing, basic computer networks and team delivery. The final project emphasized written requirements, API design, data integrity and peer review. No professional certification is claimed. Reads English technical documentation and can explain a familiar implementation in a short written summary.

input.text: Synthetic training reference: PostgreSQL transactions group related changes so that either all changes commit or none become visible. A booking API should validate the requested slot, check the authenticated owner and insert the reservation inside a transaction. A uniqueness constraint is necessary to prevent two concurrent requests from booking the same slot. Application code should translate a conflict into a clear response and avoid claiming success before commit. A useful integration test opens two concurrent transactions, submits the same slot, and verifies that exactly one reservation exists. Tests should also cover rollback after validation or downstream failure. Log a correlation identifier rather than personal booking content. This invented reference is used only as an embedding input sample and is not a verified citation or an external learning URL.
